transcript.content: Hi, I’m glad you came in today. What brings you in?

I just don’t care about my painting or the garden anymore, and the things I used to look forward to feel like a burden. It is very hard for me to get motivated to do anything these days, and I just feel so weary.
Have you had other times in your life when you felt depressed like this for weeks or months and then got better in between, or has this low mood been more or less constant for at least two years?

No, I haven't really experienced a low mood like this before in my life. This current heavy feeling has only been going on for the last few months, so it definitely hasn't been a constant thing for two years.

When you’re feeling at your lowest, have you had any hallucinations or very strong beliefs that others say aren’t true, such as hearing voices or feeling convinced you’ve done something unforgivable? Have you also had any thoughts of ending your life?
No, I haven't had any of those kinds of experiences, even when I'm feeling very low. I don't hear voices, hold any strange beliefs, or have thoughts of ending my life.
How has your sleep been over the past few months—are you sleeping much more or less than usual, or waking very early? Have you also noticed any change in your appetite or weight?

Lately, food feels like a chore and I have to remind myself to eat, so my daughter has noticed my clothes are hanging looser on me. As for sleep, during that busy spell in the spring, my mind would race with ideas at night making it hard to rest, and I was also sleeping less to manage my husband's care.

During that busy spell in the spring, did you feel unusually energetic or euphoric, more talkative or confident than usual, and need much less sleep without feeling tired? Did others notice you were acting differently or unusually driven?

Yes, back in the spring I felt strangely revved up, overly cheerful, and so confident that I believed I had a special gift to fix our whole senior program. I talked so fast that I would constantly interrupt others, and my mind raced with so many ideas at night that I couldn't sleep, yet I felt like I had endless energy. My daughter and the other volunteers definitely noticed and kept telling me to slow down because I was acting so driven and unlike myself.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient currently has a depressive episode marked by anhedonia, low motivation, fatigue, reduced appetite, and weight loss over the last few months. Crucially, she also reports a prior distinct spring episode with elevated/overly cheerful mood, increased confidence/grandiosity, pressured speech, racing thoughts, decreased need for sleep, increased energy, and noticeable change in behavior observed by others, consistent with a manic/hypomanic syndrome. There are no psychotic symptoms in the current depressive state. This pattern supports bipolar affective disorder, current episode mild or moderate depression.
